units.title: Communities

subtopics.title: Communities

outcomes.text: Students will encounter a sympathetic native speaker and interpret their ability to communicate effectively. (Latin excluded)
Students will explain the importance of culture and acquisition of the target language in a 21st century global economy.
Students will identify connections between target language and another content area using either English or the target language.
Students will use their knowledge of the target language to identify and make connections with specialized vocabulary used in various professions.

units.title: Comparisons of Practices, Products, and Perspectives

topics.title: Comparisons of Practices, Products, and Perspectives

subtopics.title: Comparisons of Practices, Products, and Perspectives

outcomes.text: Students will compare the target language with English to better understand language systems.
Students will describe practices and perspectives of a culture(s) in which the target language is spoken.
Students will explain how products, practices, and perspectives of a culture in which the target language is spoken contribute to the culture in which the student lives.

Students will explain how products such as political structures, historical artifacts, literature, and/or visual and performing arts reflect the perspectives of a culture(s) in which the target language is spoken.
Students will identify and explain how perspectives of a culture(s) are related to practices of a culture(s) in which the target language is spoken, referencing authentic materials.

units.title: Interpersonal Communication

subtopics.title: Interpersonal Communication

outcomes.text: Students will be able to ask and respond to questions about familiar topics based on their own lives and interests.
Students will be able to comprehend and apply vocabulary in appropriate contexts when engaged in conversations and correspondence.
Students will be able to express and elicit feelings and emotions in the target language.
Students will be able to provide and exchange detailed information on familiar topics in formal and informal social situations.

units.title: Interpretive Communication

subtopics.title: Interpretive Communication

outcomes.text: Classical languages only- students will provide literal translations of Latin and ancient Greek texts. Responses are in English.
Students will apply comprehension strategies to interpret text.
Students will identify main ideas, topics and specific information in a variety of authentic auditory and written materials.

units.title: Presentational Communication

subtopics.title: Presentational Communication

outcomes.text: Students will deliver oral presentations related to the culture in which the target language is spoken.
Students will narrate stories about experiences or events familiar to them orally.
Students will read authentic passages aloud with appropriate pronunciation, phrasing and intonation.
Students will write narrative and expository/ informational compositions in the target language.

units.title: Communication: Students communicate in the target language

subtopics.title: Students engage in simple conversations to provide and obtain information and to express feelings and emotions by creating simple sentences and/or strings of sentences. Students of modern languages use pronunciation and intonation patterns or use appropriate non-manual markers (ASL), which are comprehensible to speakers accustomed to interacting with language learners

outcomes.text: Ask and answer a variety of questions on familiar topics, orally or in sign language, and in writing.
Participate in conversations on a variety of everyday topics to meet personal needs.
Give and respond to directions and commands, orally or in sign language, and in writing.
Exchange information in writing about familiar topics.

subtopics.title: Students comprehend brief conversations, narratives, and recorded material in familiar contexts

outcomes.text: Identify main ideas, topics, and details from simple oral/signed and written texts.
Identify main ideas, topics, and details from simple written texts.

subtopics.title: Students use simple sentences and strings of simple sentences to produce short oral/signed and written presentations based on familiar topics and including a level of accuracy in form and pronunciation that could be understood by speakers accustomed to interacting with language learners

outcomes.text: Write/sign messages using a prescribed, culturally-appropriate format.
Produce and present simple creative works orally or in sign language, and in writing.
Convey personal preferences or information pertaining to everyday life orally or in sign language, and in writing.
Create written products based on a given topic.
Read aloud from adapted texts with appropriate intonation and pronunciation.

subtopics.title: Students compare the target language with English in order to better understand language systems

outcomes.text: Compare basic grammatical structures and syntax between languages.
Compare idiomatic expressions between languages.
Compare pronunciation systems between languages.
Recognize that there are regional and/or historical variations in spoken/signed language.
Explain connections between languages through the identification of cognates.

units.title: Cultures: Students demonstrate an understanding of a culture(s) in which the target language is spoken

subtopics.title: Students describe practices of a culture(s) and perspectives of a culture(s) in which the target language is spoken

outcomes.text: Describe examples of common beliefs of a culture(s) in which the target language is spoken.
Describe common attitudes of a culture(s) in which the target language is spoken.
Describe common similarities and differences related to practices of a culture(s) in which the target language is spoken.

subtopics.title: Products and Perspectives

outcomes.text: Students identify and explain the significance of objects used in daily life, works of art, or historical artifacts that reflect the perspectives of a culture(s) in which the target language is spoken.

subtopics.title: Students recognize and compare perspectives related to products and practices of a culture(s) in which the target language is spoken to the cultural perspectives of the culture in which the student lives

outcomes.text: Compare verbal and non-verbal communication in a culture(s) in which the target language is spoken to communication in the culture in which the student lives.
Recognize contributions of a culture(s) in which the target language is spoken to life in the United States including foods, celebrations, dress, and/or architecture.

units.title: Connections: Students expand their knowledge by connecting their study of a world language(s) with other content areas

subtopics.title: Students apply information acquired in other Learning Results content areas to further their knowledge and skills in the target language

outcomes.text: Use the writing process learned in English Language Arts when writing for the target language class.
Apply research skills to further knowledge in the target language.
Apply knowledge from other Learning Results content areas including literature, social studies, science and technology, and/or the visual and performing arts to tasks in the world language classroom.

subtopics.title: Students locate authentic resources, available only through sources in the target language, and identify ideas about a culture(s) in which the target language is spoken

outcomes.text: Locate media or other authentic sources from the target language and a culture(s) in which the target language is spoken and identify a perspective and/or practice of a culture(s) different from the students' own viewpoints and/or behaviors.

outcomes.text: Interact in a variety of social situations including formal and informal personal exchanges and/or phone inquiries.
